text:
Nitrogen top-dressing (ការដាក់ជីបំប៉ន) with urea (ជីអ៊ុយសេ) can be timed using a simple fixed schedule based on the rice variety's growth duration and on whether the crop was transplanted (ស្រូវប្តាំ) or direct-seeded (ស្រូវព្រោះ), as an alternative to Leaf Color Chart (LCC)-based timing.

First application (ការប្រើជីលើកទី១):
- Transplanted rice: apply about 12-15 days after transplanting for short-duration/early varieties (ពូជស្រូវស្រាល), or about 25-30 days after transplanting for medium- and long-duration/photoperiod-sensitive varieties (ពូជស្រូវកណ្តាល និងស្រូវធ្ងន់).
- Direct-seeded rice: apply about 20-25 days after germination for short-duration varieties, or about 30-35 days after germination for medium/long-duration varieties.
- Illustrative rate: roughly 25-40 kg of urea per hectare (treat as a general range, not an exact prescription; check current local extension guidance or the original source before deciding a field rate).
- Apply when standing water in the field is shallow, about 3-5 cm deep, so the fertilizer is not immediately flushed away.

Second application (ការប្រើជីលើកទី២):
- Apply at the panicle initiation stage, before flower/panicle emergence (មុនកើតផ្កា).
- Illustrative rate: again roughly 25-40 kg of urea per hectare.
- Apply when standing water is deeper, about 10-15 cm, which the source associates with better fertilizer uptake and less loss.

Why correct timing and dose matter for climate resilience: this source frames nitrogen management explicitly as a climate-adaptation practice. Over-applying nitrogen produces soft, lush leaf growth that is more vulnerable to pest and disease outbreaks, particularly during the sensitive window around 30 days after crop establishment, and can leave the crop less tolerant of weather stress generally. Applying the right amount at the right growth stage instead supports more even tillering and a stronger, more uniform stand.

Note: this fixed-schedule method is simpler than, and a possible alternative to, the Leaf Color Chart-based nitrogen timing approach already covered in fertilizer_ssnm_nitrogen_timing.json; farmers or extension agents may choose either depending on what tools (e.g. an LCC card) are available to them.
